title: Activation Cadence Field Manual
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-oriented playbook for product ops leads running activation sprints (0 -> 100k users) and periodic launches across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. It combines a lightweight KPI sprintboard, simple signal definitions, and an operational readiness checklist with decision heuristics for fast go/no-go calls.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: product-ops leads, launch commanders, oncall engineers, solutions engineering liaisons.
- Scope: pre-launch 3-week activation window through the first 90 days post-rollout. Focused on throughput/cost/quality balance rather than marketing metrics.

Quick start (3-step):
1) Load the sprintboard template (row: route/model; cols: week, TTP10, MCSL, RHI, FRS) and populate with baseline values from last 7 days.
2) Run a 60-minute go/no-go sync with owners for the top 5 risk signals (see Risk Signal Priority).
3) Execute canary with 0.5% traffic and validate RHI > 0.85, MCSL < 220ms, and C1K-p95 within budget tolerance. If any fail, engage rollback or fallback routing.

KPI glossary (operator-first names):
- TTP10 (Token-Throughput per 10s): tokens served / 10s window at p50. Use for capacity planning and burst detection.
- MCSL (Median Cold-Start Latency): median latency for requests that require model spin-up (ms). Useful for serverless/dedicated pool decisions.
- C1K-p95 (Cost per 1k tokens at p95): estimated unit cost at the upper load percentile; includes batching and cache efficiency adjustments.
- RHI (Rollout Health Index): composite 0-1 score computed as (0.4*availability + 0.3*latency_health + 0.3*quality_pass_rate). Thresholds: green >=0.9, amber 0.75-0.9, red <0.75.
- FRS (Fallback Readiness Score): checklist-derived 0-1 score measuring fallback routes, model variant sync, and runbook triggerability.

Lightweight sprintboard layout (CSV-ready, copy into sheet):
route,model,week_start,baseline_TTP10,baseline_MCSL_ms,baseline_C1K_p95_usd,RHI_baseline,FRS_baseline,owner,notes
/api/generate,gpt-j-6b,2024-11-18,4200,180,0.45,0.88,0.9,platform-eng,"baseline includes cache warmups"
/api/summary,open-l3,2024-11-18,1600,240,0.62,0.81,0.8,solutions-eng,"sensitive to prompt length"

Decision heuristics (fast checks for go/no-go):
- Green: All three metrics (RHI >= 0.9, MCSL within target, C1K-p95 <= budgeted) -> proceed with ramp.
- Amber: RHI 0.8-0.9 or single metric breach -> hold for mitigation window (2–6 hours), escalate if no improvement.
- Red: RHI < 0.75 or cascading latency plus error-rate -> pause rollout, switch to fallback model or region, run incident triage.

Risk Signal Priority (top 7, with owner role):
1) Eviction storm on KV cache (owner: infra)
2) Autoscaler oscillation (owner: platform-eng)
3) P95 tail latency climb (>2x baseline) (owner: serving-runtime)
4) Quality regression on prompt set (owner: research/qa)
5) Unexpected cost spike in C1K-p95 (owner: finance-ops)
6) Authentication or quota errors (owner: security)
7) Customer Affected Rate > 0.5% (owner: customer-success)

Mitigation primitives (actionable snippets):
- Throttle: apply route-level token throttle -10% for 15m, monitor RHI.
- Fallback: switch router policy to model-variant-low-cost (warm cache) with 1s grace delay.
- Split: shift 10% of traffic to Dedicated pool in region with reserved capacity.
- Rollback token: revert new model binary with traffic shift to last-stable tag and run quick quality smoke.

Readiness checklist (pre-canary, 24–48h):
[ ] Owners assigned and reachable (Slack + phone)
[ ] Week of runbook published and linked in rotation channel
[ ] Canary automation and traffic shaping validated in staging
[ ] RHI baseline computed and documented in sprintboard
[ ] FRS >= 0.8 (fallback endpoints healthy)
[ ] Cost guardrails set (alerting at +25% projected burn)
[ ] Data plane logging and tracing enabled + retention for first 7 days
[ ] Escalation matrix with SRE oncall and product-ops lead

Canary execution play (0.5% -> 5% over 6 hours):
- T=0 start: deploy canary (0.5%), validate smoke (5-10 minutes). Check basic health.
- T+30m: compare RHI vs baseline, inspect KV cache hit-rate. If RHI delta < -0.05 continue.
- T+90m: move to 2% if metrics stable. If amber, hold and run mitigations.
- T+6h: if green, proceed to ramp plan (5% -> 25% next day).

Post-launch first 72h (what to watch):
- Hourly RHI and C1K-p95, automated alerts to #launch-ops when RHI dips below 0.82.
- Daily quality sample of 200 responses across user segments; target quality_pass_rate >= 94%.
- Cost reconciliation at 24h and 72h windows, compare to forecast.

Templates and quick links (placeholders to replace with actual artifacts before launch):
- Sprintboard template: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-2345/sprintboard (copy and populate)
- Runbook stub: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/activation-stub.md
- Incident play: JIRA-PRODOPS-982 (incident template)

Notes from prior activations (operational lessons):
- Warm caches are the highest leverage for cost and latency; always validate prefix caching with synthetic probes.
- Small model variant mismatches caused >30% quality drop in one beta—add model signature verification to canary gating.
- Autoscaler hysteresis tuning prevented three premature scale-ups during an early ramp; apply a 3-minute hold for scale decisions in the first 24h.

Appendix: sample RHI calculation (operator-friendly):
- availability = (1 - error_rate_5m) clipped to [0,1]
- latency_health = 1 - min( (p95_latency - target_p95) / (2*target_p95), 1 )
- quality_pass_rate = fraction of sample prompts passing eval threshold
- RHI = 0.4*availability + 0.3*latency_health + 0.3*quality_pass_rate

Contact and ownership: Asha Patel (product-ops) primary author; cross-check with platform-eng and serving-runtime before scheduling activation.

Change log (short):
- 2024-08-22: initial draft and sprintboard template added.
- 2024-10-03: added RHI metric and canary cadence updates after Q3 activations.
- 2024-11-12: refined heuristics and updated mitigation primitives.

End of manual.
